en: From the Great Avataṃsaka Treasury flow forth boundless myriad practices with their various distinctions. It opens the gates of expedient means, cultivating illusion through illusion;
the numinous light shines through, and the six characteristics are all empty. This is the inconceivable realm of Sudhana’s southern journey.
There was a venerable master named Zhong, who, using the samādhi of the pen, sported in supernatural powers to conjure this [work].
All these marks are like images reflected in a mirror; the *rūpakāya* appears before one.

If a person contemplates in this way and resolves with such faith, they shall behold the Bhikṣu Guṇamegha face-to-face without even rising from their seat. From the moment he first resolved his mind [on enlightenment], he has already entered into harmony with Mañjuśrī.
I was requested to compose a preface for him. How could I wish to remain silent? This was written by Pan Xingsi of Yingyang.
Illustration (of the Guardian Devas, etc.
from the *Gaṇḍavyūha-parivarta* of the *Avataṃsaka-sūtra*: The Transformation Scene of Sudhana’s Pilgrimage.
At that time, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva spoke in verse:
The Awakening Flower first blooms to the east of the City of Awakening; I bow my head to Mañjuśrī, who has completely dispelled all delusions.
After traveling through a hundred cities, the Stone Man claps his hands and laughs at the spring breeze.
(Portrait of Mañjuśrī)
Thereupon, Sudhana spoke in verse:
Seeking a spiritual friend atop the peak of Mount Sumeru, I gaze toward the south, north, east, and west—how far does it extend?
The Cloud of Virtue comes from a distant mountain; I pay homage to his manifestation in a thousand million bodies.
Illustration (Dechen):
At that time, Sudhana recited these verses:
"Between the waves, transformation-buddhas sit upon lotuses; Already, layer upon layer, they have scattered the sand."
Do not advance further to seek wondrous enlightenment; It is sufficient simply to return home right here.
*Painting of Sudhana’s Gradual Progress* (Haiyun). The verse says:
Moving and returning through the void, he manifests his entire body; appearing and disappearing with ease, he daily reveals the true Dharma.
All dharmas ultimately return to the root of non-abiding; understanding that there is neither Buddha nor person, he paints this image. (Shanzhu)
The youth Sudhana traveled south by stages. A verse says:
Seated loftily upon a lion amidst the bustling marketplace, Ten thousand celestial hosts pay homage to his compassionate countenance.
Maitreya suddenly entered the principle of perfect penetration, Sitting and listening as warbling orioles sing through the chaotic mountains.
The Portrait (Mega):
Sudhana the Youth travels southward by stages. A verse says:
The gates of liberation open, reaching everywhere; An old fisherman on Xie’s family boat.
A mere twelve years have passed since arriving; let the thousand sages stand downwind before this portrait.
(Liberation) Sudhana the Youth gradually travels along; the verse says:
Sāgaradhvaja entered meditative absorption for many days; From beneath his feet he radiated light, all of it swift and rapid.
The youth asked earnestly about both ends: The painted image of the *Mahāprajñāpāramitā* (Sāgaradhvaja).
The youth Sudhana traveled south by stages. A verse says:
In the northeastern corner of the sea, The layman Śūradatta dwells upon a high lotus in a grove.
He clearly reveals to me the nature of True Suchness: Merit is never in vain; the fruit is not empty.
The verse for the painted image (of Hevajra/Heṣa) says:
Clad in deer skin, with grass for his shroud, Within the sage’s flask, there is another autumn.
Holding hands, we traveled together to places of scenic appreciation; in a single moment, we traversed Buddha-fields as numerous as the sands of the Ganges.
(Vimokṣa) composed this verse:
[The verse follows]
The youth sought out the Master Śaṇṭha; At his gate, a distinct air of a singular tradition was revealed.
Only after ascending the mountain of blades and entering the mass of fire Did he suddenly awaken to the perfect luminosity that form is emptiness. (Śaṇṭha)
The verse says:
In the city of Vejayanta is the maiden Maitrāyaṇī, Her skin a deep violet, a mass of golden light;
The path to the Vairocana-garbha palace is clearly defined, And the young boy walks straight along it.
The verse for the painted image (of Maitreya’s compassionate conduct) says:
"Vipaśyin once said: 'In a future life, I shall practice the path following after as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges.'"
One should simply know how to follow the wisdom of the lamp-light, regardless of what bystanders may say regarding the merits of this or that painting.
The verse in the *Sudarsana* states:
A gathering of ten thousand youths played together on the banks of the Sha River;
Mañjuśrī accepted my counting and writing— two fives make one ten—
and painted this image (of the Lord of Sovereignty).
The verse says:
Within this house of mine is but a single vessel; Whatever the vessel desires is fulfilled as wished.
This is called the liberation door of the inexhaustible treasury; Cease further agitation and seek the prediction of enlightenment.
The verse (complete) for the painted image says:
Five hundred devas play various musical instruments, Yet none can rival the lute without strings of the householder.

Lightly strumming a single melody of the patience of non-arising, The pure breeze from all eight directions refreshes the traveler’s breast. A Hymn on the Portrait (by Myōchi): The patience of non-arising is lightly strummed as a single melody;
The pure breeze from all eight directions refreshes the traveler’s breast. A Hymn on the Portrait (by Myōchi).
Ratnaśikhin received Sudhana with earnest hospitality; returning home, they walked hand-in-hand to view the pavilions and terraces.
(19) Having long conveyed the fragrant message, she would not open [the door] unless she recognized the voice.
[The portrait of Ratnaśikhin.]
The verse says:
In the City of Universal Eyes, all blended fragrances Upon contact, their rich aroma instantly brings coolness;
Though they are neither aloeswood nor dragon-castor musk, They draw forth the praise of the devas as something extraordinary.
The verse for the painted image (Universal Eye) says:
"The king’s majesty and the jailer’s wrath— Carving the heart and splitting the belly, they bring such great sorrow to man."
Hesitatingly, he was led into the Hall of Non-arising; a single song [resounded] as the peaches and plums blossomed in the rear garden.
(The Portrait of King Anabhibhū) The verse says:
Great King Mahāprabha within the City of Sublime Light, Seated high upon his jeweled throne by the roadside— Young man, there is no need for you to knock and ask repeatedly.
This is the portrait of Xie Sanlang on his fishing boat. (Mahāprabha)
The Verse says:
How marvelous is the laywoman Acalā! Her supernormal powers are manifold;
when emerging from samādhi, She inquires whether Sudhana has returned, Like the single orb of the bright moon reflected in a celestial lake.
The verse for the painted image (Acala) says:
The sun rises in the east and sets in the west at night; From atop the city wall, one gazes afar when the moon is bright.
Do not say that non-Buddhists lack ingenuity; on the mountain peak, he alone slowly leans upon his staff.
(The verse by Pien-hsing [Viśvāmitra] says:)
The elder’s skillful method for selling incense is excellent; it can sever all afflictions.
This essential transmission of news is not something to be bartered. It is a single stalk of grass held in Mañjuśrī’s hand—a painted image of the *utpala* flower.
The verse says:
Observe the gathering and dispersing of mists, clouds, and seasonal vapors; At the gateway of the sea, coming and going without weary hesitation.
When a single sail is raised by the wind, the boat arrives; Swiftly it carries the traveler to the further shore.
The verse for the painted image (of Vasiṣṭha) says: In the city of Rāmāvatī,
the Supreme Victor— Upon seeing him, Sudhana gave rise to joy and celebration.
Hundred thousand householders always follow him; a single grain of divine elixir can cure all diseases.
(The Unsurpassed Victorious One) Verse:
The Lion’s Yawn, Liu Tiemo—how many heroes have there been in antiquity and today?
Even if you were granted the privilege of seeing Śākyamuni face-to-face, he would summon you before him in a single indictment to share in his retribution.
(Hark! The Portrait. (The Lion’s Yawn.)
The Verse says:
The youth seeks bird tracks in the void; In every step he beholds Vāsukī’s playful grace.
Together they gaze upon the spring in the rear garden; A thousand eyes suddenly open like the sun over a thousand worlds.
The Verse on the Portrait (of the Woman Vāsulī):
Nirvāṇa, Parinirvāṇa, and Non-parinirvāṇa; Time, Earth, Withered Tree, and Entwined Tangle.
How can it compare to the sudden awakening to perfect penetration?
I prostrate to the painted image of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva (Vaiśravaṇa).
The verse says:
A cool cascade flows amidst dense thickets; Light mountain flowers rest upon emerald bamboos.
The Great Being Avalokiteśvara dwells in their midst; The youth gazes upward with eyes wide open at the painted image. (Avalokiteśvara)
The verse says:
The primary cause for attaining the Dharma arises from universal excellence; Through the universal gate, one swiftly practices for a long time.
The land from which [the Buddha] comes is inquired about according to its true nature; Look at my eyebrows—how many hairs do they have?
The Verse on the Portrait (Saddharmābhisamaya):
In the Palace of the King of Emptiness, the Sole Vessel of Mahādeva, He scooped up the waters of the ocean to wash his face.
Śākyamuni, sixteen feet in height, Even when halved and divided three times,
his painted image is not yet seen. (The Great Deity) The verse says:
In this place, you, O Lord, have long planted seeds of merit; The treasure-store of your house shall remain with you forever.
Clearly today it is entrusted once more, So that you may not be one who fails to reach their destination along the way. (Painting: Anjuju)
The Verse says:
Body clad in vermilion robes, wearing the Brahma crown, A brilliant cluster of constellations gathered upon one person.
Before the wind and beneath the moon, as if meeting face-to-face— This would make Official Xie of Caozhou laugh to death!
The Verse on the Portrait (Saṃpādyanti) says:
On a cool night, the moonlight is perfectly full; The Lord of the Night Deities speaks of the conditions for awakening.
Depart, depart; there is no need for further discourse. *The Archery of Double Fists Outside the Vajra Gate* (by Pude Jingguang).
The verse says:
There is a night goddess named Joyful Eyes, Who emanates clouds of compassion from her body in countless billions;
She benefits sentient beings in accordance with their faculties and dispositions, A feat that truly relies upon the power of her compassion and patience.
[Portrait: Joyful Eyes Contemplating]
The Verse says:
The Night Goddess constantly radiates light from her white tuft; Extending from between her brows, it illuminates the ten directions.
This was not a mere provisional manifestation for Sudhana; Now, throughout the entire world, she has never been hidden.
The verse for the painted image (Universal Savior of Beings with Wondrous Virtue) says:
In every thought-moment, vast wisdom is born; In every atom, boundless meanings are proclaimed.
The Night Goddess Śāntasvaranirghoṣa, who once received the prophecy from the Buddha Kuṭaṅga,
has a painted image [of her].
The verse says:
Speech and sounds are the dust of the auditory faculty; when one emerges from this dust, hearing is itself the True Reality.
When a guest arrives at the door and you do not recognize them, a yellow oriole sings its first note upon a branch.
(The Protector of All Cities)
The verse says:
The golden crow sinks in the west, the moonlight fades; The vast earth lies in a dream from which one has not yet awakened.
An old man comes to the side of the pillow, Laughing loudly two or three times, "He-he!"
The verse for the painted image (*citrapaṭa*) [titled] "The Blossoming of All Tree Flowers" says:
"The Night Goddess who Protects and Saves Sentient Beings, Scattering precious jewels upon a seat of jewel-flowers."
Carrying his own flask, he went to buy village wine; Returning in his robe, he came to act as the host.
(The Power of Great Vow and Diligence) The verse says:
The Tathāgata’s family and kingdom pervade the Sahā world; do you not see them in the south, north, east, and west?
If the youth wishes to know the conduct of a bodhisattva, he should further inquire of Gopā on the path ahead.
(Miaode Yuanman) [The Painting]
The Verse says:
The youth first ascends the great lecture hall; A hundred thousand palace deities come forward to welcome him.
Gradually he beholds the maiden Gopā; He raises a clay ox with a roar—a scene of laughter!
The verse for the painted image (Gopā) says:
"The little servant of the Tathāgatas of the three times, Born from me through inconceivable means."

On a cool night facing the moon, I lightly snap my fingers; I offer this verse in praise of the precious image of Māyā’s great belly (Māyādevī): Verse: On a cool night facing the moon, I lightly snap my fingers;
I offer this verse in praise of the precious image of Māyā’s great belly (Māyādevī).
He traveled to the Heaven of the Thirty-three; The celestial maidens spoke of its profound mysteries with earnest devotion.
Sudhana sought him out without wearying of the toil; It was as if his feet never touched the ground.
(By Tianzhuyouguang)
The verse says:
As a youth, he traveled far to seek out friends; He mastered all arts and succeeded his predecessor.
Chanting and upholding the alphabet, he entered perfect clarity; A distinct tradition, its scenery most exquisite.
The verse on the painted image (*Vasumitra-sarva-śilpa*) says:
Next, one enters the various sublime samādhis; In these matters, there is fundamentally no partiality.
Thank you for your kind instructions on the origins of awakening; unable to remain, I must take the road once more and bid you farewell.
[The image of] *Bhadraśilpa* (Skilled in All Arts) offers this verse: Verse:
I know that your liberation is called "non-attachment," yet the green bamboos and yellow flowers remain unextinguished.
If you seek and investigate without reaching its source, it is merely a case of wandering in vain.
(Portrait: [Upright and firm] liberation.)
The verse says:
Within this very city, Sudhana visited Candracchattra; having seen him, he was filled with joy.
The radiance within the house was exceedingly brilliant, and the boy, as before, obtained a single wooden peg.
The verse for the painted image (Wondrous Moon) says:
The transmission of immeasurable Buddhas is an inexhaustible treasury; From this inexhaustible treasury arises an inexhaustible manifestation.
Rootless, fundamentally empty, and without support, Because there is nothing to be attained,
it becomes the unsurpassed painted image.
(By Ajita) The verse says:
The Brahmin stayed only to the south of the city; Undaunted by the arduous journey, he went alone to attend upon him.
Having heard his words of sincere aspiration, He came to know through faith that the Buddhas do not vanish into empty talk. (Śānti)
The verse says:
A young girl and a young boy, their bones and eyes fresh, Lead by hand a sturdy jade steed;
With earnest intent they come to report the path of Sudhana: "The road before Maitreya’s tower is most intimate."
The Verse on the Portrait (of Guṇakarī):
Having traveled through all directions, I am gradually returning; Suddenly, I encounter one who has obtained a magnificent pavilion.
Lifting my head, Maitreya lightly snapped his fingers; Suddenly, the eyes of my entire life were opened wide.
A verse on the painted image (of Maitreya):
Before the temple of the Ancient Buddha, I received his entrustment;
Seeking a spiritual friend among humans and in the heavens, I thank the Purple-Gold Radiant Arm for renewing my vows.
I bow my head to Mañjuśrī of Great Wisdom Power. (Seeing Mañjuśrī again)
The Verse says:
Walking while drumming and playing the lute, Returning him to his own home. The wooden child can grasp the stone;
The barren woman knows how to brew tea. Clouds disperse and the moon appears at the edge of the sky; Spring comes and flowers bloom upon the trees.
"Good Wealth visits the Universal Bases; beans piled up without sprouting" (the painting of Samantabhadra).
Recently, while reading the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*, I reached the "Chapter on the Youth Śrīkūṭa and the Maiden Śrīmatī," according to Master Qingliang’s commentary.

Master Li’s Exposition on the Meaning of the Teachings: Having examined it closely yet not fully understood, I reflected upon it repeatedly until suddenly there was a realization. I composed this verse:
"The wondrous intent of the *kumārabhūta* stage is gathered at the end; Sudhana has now reached his destination and ceased his southern journey."
Suddenly and completely entering the treasury of Vairocana, I now regret having previously sought monks on other mountains.
Now, because the Elder of Yanqing has brought me the painted *Avataṃsaka* transformation tableaux and the fifty-two verses to show me,
I have recorded these preceding verses at the end of the scroll to fulfill their intended meaning.
The eleventh day of the intercalary second month in the fourth year of the Shaosheng era. Written by Zhang Shangying, Governor of Hongzhou.
Huang Tingjian, Proofreader at the Jixian Academy, bows his head once:
"Master artisans are able to paint all things within the world; The ten directions and three periods of time are created solely by the mind."
Fifty-three gates, one single lock: I and Sudhana together traveled everywhere, Entering all realms like illusions and dreams.
The true rules for studying the Way, The wondrous virtue of Bodhi, and the mind of birth-and-death— All appear as layered reflections in the Great Perfect Mirror.
I have heard that Li Bashi painted this Transformation Sutra, yet I have not seen it. Bashi was fond of learning and excelled in clerical script and small seal script;
his painting is the contemporary counterpart to the Master Daozi. Without having met Bashi, one can already perceive the likeness of his art in this work.
I shall surely go to follow him in his travels so as to perfect this supreme skill. Inscribed by Su Ziyou of Meishan.
In the ninth month of the third year of the Shaosheng era, the Elder Foyin came from Yunju to visit me at Gaoyang and brought this [work] for me to see.
Su Dongpo remarked, "Master Zhong’s brushwork resembles that of Li Bashi; this is merely an observation of his painting. To which I replied:
Master Zhong’s work is not merely a painting; he simply sought to follow in the footsteps of the legacy of Xuanzang, roaming at ease within the Dharma-realm.
Those who view it later need not rise from their seats to behold, as if from the eastern outskirts of the City of Enlightenment (Bodhgayā), the Elephant King Mañjuśrī turning back.
Having spent his life seeking virtuous friends to the south and traversing a hundred cities, the merit accumulated over kalpas is realized all at once.
[End. This so-called "Opening of the Gate of Great Giving" could not possibly be fully exhausted even by painting it during the age of the Final Dharma.
On the twentieth day of the tenth month of the *Bingsi* year of the Shaoxing era, this colophon was written by the Great Master Foyin (Liaoyuan) at Wolong Hermitage.
On the ninth day of the fourth month of the third year of Kenchō, at the Thatched Hermitage of Jichiku-in, [this was transcribed] from the copy held in the room of Seiganbō.
I have completed the transcription of the Tang edition of the *Sudhana-avadāna* (Good House) that I consulted.
Although that manuscript contained both illustrations and the scriptural text, I have omitted them for the time being.
By virtue of the roots of goodness from having seen, heard, and rejoiced in this, may I surely accomplish that great function of the realization of suchness through understanding and practice.
Beginning with the four debts of gratitude and extending to all classes of beings throughout the Dharma-realm, taking my present life as the foundation until the end of the future,
may I universally receive the protection and empowerment of spiritual friends, and together enter the ocean of the fruit of Vairocana.
Śramaṇa Shi Xinhai of the Avataṃsaka School’s Final Generation.
